items.title: Bitdeer Sells All 281 Bitcoin It Mined Last Week, Holds None
items.summary:
Bitcoin Magazine 

Bitdeer Sells All 281 Bitcoin It Mined Last Week, Holds None 

Bitdeer sold every bitcoin it mined last week and still holds none of its own, the company said in its latest weekly update, continuing a nearly year-long strategy of turning production into cash after a weekend plunge in the bitcoin price.

The Singapore-based miner reported output of 281.1 BTC and sales of 281.1 BTC for the week, for a net addition of zero. Its pure holdings, which exclude customer deposits, were zero as of Nov. 20.

The sales came as bitcoin fell to a weekend low of $55,106 early Saturday at 1:17 AM ET, Bitcoin Magazine Pro data shows. The price has since bounced to near $62,700 as of 11:23 AM ET Monday.

Bitdeer’s reserve has been drained all year 

Bitdeer’s treasury shrank from roughly 2,000 BTC at the end of 2025 to zero by Feb. 20, when Bitcoin Magazine reported the miner had liquidated its reserve over eight weeks. At the time, the company said the move should not be a concern for the broader market.

Bitdeer’s filings show how little it has kept since. In its third-quarter results, filed with the SEC on a Form 6-K on Nov. 10, the company listed 47 BTC held at Sept. 30, down from 2,029 a year earlier.

Its September production update showed 61 BTC held at the end of August. The company mined 1,355 BTC in September and 3,855 BTC in the third quarter, compared with 1,109 BTC in the same quarter of 2025.

Self-mining margins stay thin 

Bitdeer has grown its fleet quickly. Self-mining hashrate reached 82.3 exahashes per second in the third quarter, up from 35.0 a year…

items.title: Solo Bitcoin Miner Wins $191,000 Block Reward With Just 11 TH/s
items.summary:
Bitcoin Magazine 

Solo Bitcoin Miner Wins $191,000 Block Reward With Just 11 TH/s 

A solo miner running about 11 terahashes per second has mined Bitcoin block 977,057, collecting a reward of 3.1287 BTC, or about $191,000, on a machine that makes up roughly one-millionth of a percent of the network.

The block was found through the solo service at CKpool on Sunday, Nov. 22, at about 7:54 a.m. ET. The reward is the 3.125 BTC subsidy plus about 0.0037 BTC in transaction fees, and it was worth roughly $191,000 at bitcoin’s price when the block landed.

How the solo block played out 

The block holds 584 transactions. Its coinbase transaction pays 3.0661 BTC to a single address and 0.0626 BTC, about 2% of the reward, to a second output. That split matches the service’s 2% fee, which means the miner’s take is a little over $186,000.

Con Kolivas, the developer behind CKpool, congratulated the miner on X, whose address he abbreviated as bc1q~zy9j. It matches the end of the address that received the payout. Kolivas called it the 323rd block found on the service and “yet another lucky one.”

He said the miner had only about 11.1 TH/s of hashrate on a 3.47 TH worker. “A miner of this size has about a one in 1650 chance of solving a block in a year,” Kolivas wrote.

The block was tagged to Solo CK on the mempool.space block explorer, and its coinbase carries the pool’s signature. CKpool describes itself as a service that lets miners go after full solo blocks without running their own node, since you cannot mine directly to a Bitcoin Core node.

items.title: Nvidia Soars as Huang Returns, Lifting Stocks and Crypto Shares
items.summary:
Bitcoin Magazine 

Nvidia Soars as Huang Returns, Lifting Stocks and Crypto Shares 

Nvidia shares jumped about 35% on Monday after the chipmaker reinstated Jensen Huang as president and CEO, restoring roughly $1 trillion in market value at the open. The stock traded near $169.20 at 10:41 a.m. ET, up from Friday’s close of $125.53, and Wall Street rallied with it.

The board voted unanimously to bring Huang back, effective immediately, after what it called a series of discussions and meetings. It said it received input from “senior levels of the United States government” and is confident his return “poses no national security risk.” President Donald Trump had urged the move.

Several items remain open. An independent board committee will finish its investigation into reports that Huang was the target of a foreign intelligence effort, and Huang said he will cooperate. Nvidia also formed a national security and export control committee and is searching for a chief compliance officer.

From resignation to reversal 

Huang resigned on Nov. 11, days after admitting an affair with a woman U.S. officials believe is linked to Chinese intelligence. Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress became interim CEO and Harvey Jones became board chair. Nvidia had said it was searching for a permanent successor.

The stock slid for seven straight weeks, the longest such streak since 2008. On Friday it plunged 14% after Reuters reported that the SEC is examining the company’s accounting practices. Reuters noted that investigations are not evidence of wrongdoing. Huang’s return reverses most of…
items.t: Nvidia Soars as Huang Returns, Lifting Stocks and Crypto Shares

items.title: Cross River Bank Launches Its First Bitcoin-Backed Loans With LendingUSA
items.summary:
Bitcoin Magazine 

Cross River Bank Launches Its First Bitcoin-Backed Loans With LendingUSA 

Cross River Bank has launched its first bitcoin-backed loans, working with consumer lender LendingUSA to let eligible borrowers take out between $10,000 and $250,000 against their BTC without selling it.

The program is the first time Cross River has originated bitcoin-secured loans itself, according to The Block. LendingUSA runs the application platform, and every loan is made by Cross River, a New Jersey state-chartered bank, according to LendingUSA .

How the loans work 

Borrowers can choose a loan-to-value ratio of 30%, 50% or 70%, which sets how much cash they receive against the value of the bitcoin they pledge. LendingUSA defines the ratio as the loan balance divided by the value of the collateral, so a 50% loan against $100,000 of bitcoin would be $50,000. Two repayment options are offered: interest-only or no monthly payments.

On an interest-only loan, borrowers make smaller monthly payments that roughly cover interest, with the principal and any remaining interest due at the end of the term. On a no-monthly-payment loan, the full balance plus interest is due at the end. LendingUSA says borrowers can repay early without penalties or fees .

Applicants go through a soft credit check, and LendingUSA says approval rests on the crypto being pledged rather than a credit score. The company says funding typically arrives within one to three business days after the collateral is verified.

Custody and margin risk

items.title: Bitcoin Core Patches Node-Stall Bug Found by Block’s AI Scanner
items.summary:
Bitcoin Magazine 

Bitcoin Core Patches Node-Stall Bug Found by Block’s AI Scanner 

Bitcoin Core developers have disclosed and patched a medium-severity bug that let an attacker temporarily freeze a node’s processing of blocks and transactions, a flaw first flagged by an AI scanner built by Block’s Spiral.

The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-117348, is fixed in Bitcoin Core versions 30.5, 31.3 and 32.1. The 30.5 and 31.3 releases shipped Friday alongside the public advisory, while 32.1 has carried the fix since Oct. 27.

Affected versions run from 29.0 through 29.5, 30.0 through 30.4 and 31.0 through 31.2. The 29.x series has reached end of life and will not get a fix, so operators on that branch need to move to a newer release.

How the Core bug worked 

Bitcoin Core keeps “orphan” transactions, whose parent transactions it has not yet seen, and asks peers that announce them for the missing pieces. Since version 29.0, the software builds a list of an orphan’s parents and checks each one against its mempool and filters before deciding what to request.

A single inv message can carry up to 50,000 entries, and the software did not skip duplicates. An attacker could send a node an orphan with thousands of missing parents, then send messages repeating that transaction’s ID 50,000 times.

“Each such message stalls the node for over a dozen seconds, during which it processes no messages from other peers, including blocks,” the advisory said. Sending more messages could stretch the disruption out.

The fix makes the node process each transaction announced in an inv message…
items.t: Bitcoin Core Patches Node-Stall Bug Found by Block’s AI Scanner

items.title: UK FCA Bars Crypto Exchanges From Market Making on Their Own Venues
items.summary:
Bitcoin Magazine 

UK FCA Bars Crypto Exchanges From Market Making on Their Own Venues 

The U.K. will bar crypto exchange operators from trading against their own capital on the venues they run, while a new Treasury order clears independent market makers to trade on those platforms without a separate dealing permission.

The Financial Conduct Authority’s final rules say a firm “must not execute any orders against its proprietary capital” on a qualifying trading platform it operates. The FCA’s guidance spells out the effect: a firm “cannot act as a market maker” on its own platform. The restriction takes effect Oct. 25, 2027.

The FCA rule itself is not new. The regulator published it on June 30 in policy statement PS26/11, part of a five-document package that completed its crypto rulebook. What changed last week was the Treasury’s side of the framework.

What the FCA rule covers 

The FCA’s rulebook defines a market maker as a person who holds themselves out on a platform on a continuous basis as willing to buy and sell qualifying cryptoassets against their own capital at prices they set. That is the activity operators will be barred from on their own venues.

There is one carve-out. An operator with the appropriate permission may still engage in matched principal trading to execute client orders on its platform, as long as it follows the platform’s non-discretionary rules. The FCA warned that this model does not rule out settlement risk, so firms should take steps to minimize it.

The bar applies only to the operator’s own platform. Under the same rules, an operator with…
items.t: UK FCA Bars Crypto Exchanges From Market Making on Their Own Venues

items.title: Strategy (MSTR) Adds 457 Bitcoin for $29.6 million
items.summary:

Strategy (MSTR) Adds 457 Bitcoin for $29.6 million 

Strategy (MSTR) bought 457 bitcoin last week for $29.6 million at an average of about $64,898 per coin, an 8-K filing shows, lifting its total to 851,305 BTC as the bitcoin price trades about under the company’s average cost.

The purchase ran from Nov. 16 to Nov. 22. Strategy said it paid $64.23 billion for its stack, an average of $75,446 per coin including fees and expenses. That is $6 below the $75,452 average it reported a week earlier, so the new coins barely moved the cost basis.

The buy is also smaller than the 485 bitcoin Strategy added the week before . Strategy shares were trading near $83.50 in premarket on Monday, up about 7% from Friday’s close near $78.

How Strategy paid for the coins 

Strategy funded the purchase entirely with common stock. It sold 1,925,676 MSTR shares under its at-the-market program for net proceeds of $176.7 million, and no preferred stock was sold during the week.

Only $29.6 million of that cash went into bitcoin. The rest went to buy back Strategy’s own STRC preferred stock, which is the pattern the company has followed for several weeks.

Strategy repurchased 2,183,747 STRC shares for $211.8 million. It paid $147.0 million of that with MSTR proceeds and $64.8 million from its USD Cash balance. The preferred buyback was roughly seven times the bitcoin spend.

The board also lifted the size of its digital credit securities repurchase program from $3.0 billion to $4.0 billion. After the increase, $1.12 billion remains available. About $17.9 billion of MSTR stock…

items.title: American Bitcoin (ABTC) Lands $150 Million Bitcoin-Backed Credit Line From FalconX
items.summary:
Bitcoin Magazine 

American Bitcoin (ABTC) Lands $150 Million Bitcoin-Backed Credit Line From FalconX 

American Bitcoin Corp. (ABTC) has secured a $150 million revolving credit facility from FalconX that is backed by its bitcoin, the miner said Monday, giving it a way to raise cash without selling coins from its reserve.

The facility was signed by an American Bitcoin subsidiary and is secured by certain of the company’s bitcoin holdings. American Bitcoin said the money can go toward strategic growth opportunities and general corporate purposes. “This $150 million facility provides American Bitcoin with non-dilutive capital to support our continued operations and growth initiatives,” CEO Mike Ho said in the release.

Terms of the FalconX facility 

The FalconX line is committed up to $150 million, and each draw is subject to bitcoin collateral requirements and other customary conditions. Because it is revolving, the company can draw, repay and redraw funds during the term.

Borrowings carry a 5.95% loan fee, plus a commitment fee on any undrawn amount. The initial term is two years, with an optional three-year extension at FalconX’s discretion, subject to customary conditions. The company did not name the size of the commitment fee.

The facility has an initial collateral ratio of 143%. At that level, drawing the full $150 million would require about $214.5 million in pledged bitcoin, or roughly 3,500 BTC with bitcoin trading near $61,300 early Monday.

American Bitcoin did not say whether it has drawn on the line yet. Its release lists the risks, including the possible…
